transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Sam (Redwood); Alex, Rina, Markus, Leah, Tom (Meridian)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift, EU sovereignty pilot, and security artifacts. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We wanted to spend the first part doing a quick health check and then go into the uplift numbers and the sovereignty pilot. Sound good?
[00:18] Alex (Meridian): Yep, thanks Jordan. Quick context — we are seeing increased inference traffic from our triage pipeline, up about 2.8x month over month. So capacity is the ask, and we want the EU residency for PHI-adjacent metadata.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying q, Alex — when you say PHI-adjacent, are you storing tokens or raw notes? That affects retention and the KMS flow.
[00:47] Alex: Mostly metadata and pointers, not raw clinical notes. But our security team flagged any PII/PHI leakage risk.
[00:55] Rina (Security): Yeah that's right — we need KMS integration proof, field level encryption, and audit logs that show who accessed what model. Also are you SOC two — SOC two Type II is required for our procurement.
[01:10] Jordan: We are SOC 2 Type II, we'll share the report. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration — we call it Redwood Private KMS hookup, but sometimes the doc names are messy in transcription. We'll share the exact flow.
[01:28] Tom (ML Eng): A couple of perf things — our median latency for the 2k token flows is spiking when concurrency goes above 30. Curious what batching and KV cache options you recommend.
[01:42] Priya: Good call. For that workload we usually suggest a dedicated pool with continuous batching and prefix/KV cache enabled. There was a note in last week's bench that quantization tradeoffs gave 1.6x throughput but slightly noisier generations — we can run an eval set.
[02:02] Markus (SRE): Can you clarify the difference between dedicated and private VPC? We read the docs but want to confirm traffic egress patterns and whether the control plane sees logs.
[02:18] Priya: Yeah — Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our hosted environment with tenant isolation and SLA. Private/VPC is a customer-managed network where the control plane is still Redwood but data plane can be in your VPC or in an on-prem appliance per the private deployment model. Audit logs for private can be streamed to your SIEM — we support S3/Hum... sorry S3 and direct syslog sinks.
[02:42] Rina: When you say control plane sees logs — will any content plane payload be accessible? We need assurance that payloads don't persist in control plane logs.
[02:50] Sam (CSM): Quick interruption — in our private deployments we separate telemetry and payloads; payload metadata for routing is visible but payload bodies are not retained in control plane logs unless you enable debugging. We'll get the exact retention policy out.
[03:12] Leah (Procurement): From the procurement side, what's the pricing cliff if we do a 12 month vs 24 month committed uplift? We need numbers to model OpEx.
[03:25] Jordan: We have a three-tier commit model: small uplift (x1.5), medium (x3), large (x5) with respective discounts. For a 24-month term we can layer in an extra 8-12% discount and commit credits towards EU private pilot run time. I'll put concrete bands in the SOW.
[03:46] Alex: Sounds good. Also, timeline — we want EU pilot staged in June if possible. Is that realistic?
[03:55] Priya: It's tight but possible. For EU pilot in June we need the following ASAP: signed pilot SOW, access details for your VPC/network firewall team, and the benchmark dataset we can run to validate latency.
[04:11] Tom: For the benchmark dataset, we'll need a template. Can you provide one?
[04:18] Priya: Yes — I'll share the benchmark template and runbook. It includes sequence length distributions, load patterns, and sample prompts.
[04:26] [05:00] (background) conversation glitch — Speaker 2 overlapped, small crosstalk
[05:15] Jordan: On the contractual side, any changes to data residency or private deployments — we treat those as addenda to the base agreement; Leah, is your legal okay with an addendum approach or do you need a full contract rewrite?
[05:32] Leah: Addendum is preferred. Legal wants to see specific clauses about data residency, liability, and termination for the pilot if SLA not met.
[05:42] Rina: Also encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is non-negotiable. We need the KMS flow diagram and proof-of-concept of key rotation.
[05:55] Priya: We'll include the KMS flow and rotation schedule in the security package. Note: in our hosted dedicated we offer envelope encryption and customer KMS in most clouds; for on-prem private we support HSM integration but that requires extra ops work.
[06:15] Markus: Ops question — how do you handle failover across regions? If EU region goes flaky, will traffic failover to US and what are the data residency ramifications?
[06:28] Jordan: We can set routing policies by geo — for sovereignty constrained workloads we recommend fallback to a warm standby in a nearby EU zone. If you require strict no-failover to other geos, we can set policies that return errors instead. That's configurable.
[06:45] Alex: We're leaning toward a warm standby for reliability but only for non-PHI streams.
[07:00] Tom: On metrics, we'll need token-level cost breakdown and per-model latency slas. Can Redwood provide profiler traces?
[07:12] Priya: Yes. The Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks. We'll share sample profiler outputs. Note some of the console names in the notes may be transcribed weirdly — it's Redwood Console in the docs.
[07:30] Rina: One more security ask — can you demonstrate audit trails that tie a user identity from our SSO to model access?
[07:40] Sam: We support SAML/SSO and map identities to audit logs; we'll provide a sample trace showing identity->request->response.
[07:52] Leah: Procurement timeline: we ideally need a signed SOW by end of May to get execution in June.
[08:02] Jordan: Understood. We'll aim for SOW by May 10.
[08:08] Alex: Pricing detail — can you include committed burst capacity and burst billing rates? Our peak events require 2x baseline for 2 hours three times a month.
[08:22] Jordan: Yes — tiered burst pricing is included in the bands, and we can allocate burst pool credits for committed customers. We'll reflect that in the SOW.
[08:35] Tom: About model variants — we noticed that smaller quantized variants produced slightly more hallucinations on clinical prompts. Can you run quality regression checks?
[08:47] Priya: Absolutely — we'll run the eval set against both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants and include output diffs; if quality drops beyond threshold, we recommend using Dedicated FP16 for that route.
[09:05] (silence, note taking)
[09:12] Jordan: Ok, recap — action items for Redwood: SOW + pricing, pilot runbook, security artifacts (SOC2, KMS flow), and benchmark template. For Meridian: infra utilization reports, SOC2 scoping docs, procurement timeline confirmation.
[09:34] Leah: That's correct. Also want a follow-up deep dive with Markus and Priya about firewall and VPC peering.
[09:45] Priya: I'll schedule a 60-minute deep dive with Markus next week, proposed May 14 at 10:00 UTC.
[10:00] Alex: One last Q — any recommended guardrails for PHI-adjacent metadata tokenization so accidental leakage is reduced?
[10:10] Priya: Recommended approach: client-side redaction + tokenization, skip-contexting for sensitive fields, and strict retention policies. We'll include a short writeup.
[10:25] (brief cross talk)
[10:35] Jordan: Great. If there are no other items we'll close. Thanks all, and we'll follow up with the SOW and security package.
[10:45] Rina: Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Meeting end.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-attributed speakers, filler words, and some product names mis-typed by auto-transcribe (e.g., "Redwood Private KMS hookup" may appear as several variants).
